reason: The side rails should keep the marble from escaping the tray.
expectation: The rails will attach to the tray to guide the marble.

effect: The tray now has retaining rails, so I can work on giving it the slope needed for the marble to return.
reason: The support wedge looks like the piece that will tilt the tray.
expectation: The wedge will support the tray at a slope so the marble can roll back.

effect: The tray is now sloped, providing a way for the marble to roll back.
reason: The spring appears to belong inside the launcher to propel the marble.
expectation: The spring will make a working marble launcher.

effect: The spring is enclosed in the launcher, and I learned how its plunger and stop work. The launcher can now be fitted to the tray.
reaction: The explanation of the enclosed spring and limited push was useful.
reason: The launcher needs to be attached to the sloping tray so the player can send the marble up it.
expectation: The launcher will fit onto the tray, ready to launch the marble uphill.

effect: The launcher is attached to the sloping tray, leaving the marble to test the table.
reason: The marble should let me test whether the launch lane and slope return it to the player.
expectation: The marble will be launched and roll back down the table.

effect: The test exposed a sideways lean that traps the marble, so the tray needs levelling.
reaction: The corner trap was a useful surprise: a downhill slope alone is not enough.
reason: The thin levelling shim looks suited to correcting the sideways lean.
expectation: The shim will level the tray sideways so the marble can escape the low pocket and return.

effect: The shim corrected the low corner, and the marble now returns to the catch cup; the goal is complete.
reaction: It was satisfying to see the specific fault fixed and the return tested again.

mostWorthwhile.text: Testing the marble was most worthwhile: it revealed a sideways lean that made the return mechanism fail, rather than simply confirming the build.

leastWorthwhile.text: Attaching the launcher was straightforward progress, but less interesting than learning how it worked or testing the table.

surprise.text: I was surprised that the marble could get trapped despite the tray sloping downhill; the sideways lean made the pocket lower than its exit.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt particularly arbitrary. The shim had a clear purpose once the test exposed the low corner.

continue.text: Yes. I would be curious to see what the marble could do on its way back, especially if the next mechanism involves another test and correction.
